title: SkyByte: Architecting an Efficient Memory-Semantic CXL-based SSD with OS and Hardware Co-design
problem: CXL-based SSDs enable byte-granular memory expansion at low cost, but suffer from long flash access latency, unpredictable garbage collection stalls, and a fundamental mismatch between byte-granular CXL access and page-granular flash I/O that wastes significant bandwidth.
motivation: Main memory capacity is a critical bottleneck as datasets scale, and CXL-SSDs offer a cost-effective path, but without architectural co-design their performance gap relative to DRAM makes them impractical for latency-sensitive workloads.
method: SkyByte coordinates the host OS and SSD controller through three mechanisms. When the processor detects slow CXL-SSD accesses, the OS switches to running other threads (thread-level parallelism) to hide latency instead of stalling. The SSD controller's DRAM buffers small byte-level writes with a cacheline-level write log and page-level data cache, merging them at log cleanup time to reduce flash I/O traffic. Frequently-accessed pages are automatically promoted from the CXL-SSD to the faster host DRAM based on access frequency, together reducing stall cycles and flash I/O amplification.
key_novelty: SkyByte bridges the mismatch between byte-level CXL access and page-level flash storage by pairing OS-level context switching (the OS runs other threads during slow CXL-SSD waits) with a two-tier SSD controller DRAM buffer (cacheline-level write log and page-level data cache) that merges small writes together before they reach flash.
contributions: Opportunistic OS context switch mechanism triggered by CXL-SSD access delay detection to hide latency
Cacheline-level write log + page-level cache in SSD controller DRAM with coalescing log cleaning
Adaptive hot-page migration from CXL-SSD to host DRAM for frequently accessed data
6.11x speedup over current CXL-SSD; 23.08x reduction in flash I/O traffic; 75% of ideal DRAM performance

metrics.other: 23.08x reduction in flash chip I/O traffic; achieves 75% of ideal unlimited-DRAM performance

baselines: ideal case with unlimited host DRAM
limitations: Evaluation uses a CXL-SSD simulator rather than real hardware; latency variance from real NAND flash and GC characteristics may differ.
primary_theme: OS-hardware co-design for byte-granular CXL-SSD memory expansion efficiency
